column1: # The fix finder ("Try this setting"): when a run ends the way rule_id says, the launcher's exit notice and its "What it means" page offer this Advanced row once per game,
# while the row is still Auto for that game (FixFinder.java; dm/tools/advanced_fix.py writes the table of wiki/Troubleshooting.md from it). Tab-separated, in order of
# preference (the first row of a rule that can be offered is the one shown):
#   rule_id      an id of dm/tools/log_rules.tsv, or exit:<kind> for an end the log digest names without a matching line (LogDigest.verdict's kind, e.g. Android's own
#                low-memory exit reason with no lowmemorykiller line in the log)
#   advanced_id  a friendly or advanced row of docs/advanced_settings.tsv that the player can set (no owner); its `fixes` column names the rule
#   value        a value that row accepts
#   scope        game (set for that game only) | global (set for every game)
#   sentence     what it does and what it costs, plain, ASCII, at most 100 characters; it must follow from the switch's text in docs/env_switches.tsv or a reference entry
